# Moodie

> A tiny, deeply configurable animated SVG face for React.

Package: @moodie/react
Install: npm install https://github.com/arhxam/moodie-react/releases/latest/download/moodie-react.tgz motion
Repository: https://github.com/arhxam/moodie-react
License: MIT

## Minimal usage

```tsx
import { Moodie } from "@moodie/react";
<Moodie expression="happy" color="#5b6cff" />;
```

## Key capabilities

- 16 expressions: neutral, happy, excited, sleepy, sad, worried, thinking, love, curious, surprised, focused, cheeky, dizzy, calm, wink, alert.
- 5 shapes: circle, squircle, blob, pebble, diamond.
- Spring/tween/path morph animation, expression-specific performances, parent-canvas gaze, hover recognition, idle eye choreography, and right-click blink.
- Controlled/uncontrolled state and imperative ref methods.
- Custom normalized eye geometry.
- SSR-safe and reduced-motion aware.

## Main API

`MoodieProps`: expression, defaultExpression, expressions, expressionOrder, onExpressionChange, shape, color, eyeColor, size, eyeScale, eyeDistance, turn, flip, motion, spring, expressionMotion, eyeMotion, blink, pointer, auto, gaze, gazeLimit, clickAction, reaction, reducedMotion, ariaLabel.

Use `pointer={{ target: "parent" }}` to track across the immediate parent canvas. Configure `eyeMotion` with idle animations, hover eye/body cues, intensity, cadence, and `contextMenuBlink`. Imperative refs expose `animateEyes("wide")`.

Controlled interactive example:

```tsx
const [expression, setExpression] = useState("curious");
<Moodie expression={expression} onExpressionChange={setExpression} clickAction="random" />;
```

Use `docs/llm-guide.md` for the complete type model, accessibility rules, state mapping, custom-expression contract, and framework notes.
